tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger & Bitrus Bulus Kaze. n.d. [draft dated 2006]. A dictionary of the Izere language of Fobur: introduction (20 pp.), section 4.1 'Izere phonology'
tone_statements.quote: Izere has 29 consonant phonemes, 7 vowel phonemes and 3 level tones. ... There are five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones (LM & HL). Contour tones occur in loanwords, words with potentially onomatopoeic names such as those of birds and where a tonally dissimilar VV sequence has been shortened ... As such these synchronic occurrences are probably transitional and Izere can be regarded as having an underlying three-height system. Tones are marked as follows; HIGH acute accent above the syllable kú to die MID unmarked fa to count LOW grave accent over the syllable mì I ...

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Bitrus Bulus Kaze. n.d. [draft dated 2006]. A dictionary of the Izere language of Fobur: introduction (20 pp.), section 4.1 'Izere phonology'
sources.quote: Izere has 29 consonant phonemes, 7 vowel phonemes and 3 level tones. ... There are five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones (LM & HL). Contour tones occur in loanwords, words with potentially onomatopoeic names such as those of birds and where a tonally dissimilar VV sequence has been shortened ... sources.note: Five tones: high, mid, low, rising (LM), falling (HL); contours only in loans, bird names, shortened VV, so underlyingly three heights per the authors. Affixes bear varied tones. Nothing on stress.

sources.note: A first-hand morphological description of Izere inflection (number, tense/aspect categories). Because Izere marks noun plurality and pluractional/aspectual verb forms largely by tone alternations (as the a work listed here Blench 2000 and Erin 2022 describe, Erin citing this article), it very probably contains tone-marked paradigms and remarks on tonal inflection, but whether it states the tone inventory is unknown. Basis: title and its citation context in Erin 2022 only.
